title: Customer engagement metrics decoder and SLI table
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight, operational cheat-sheet we can attach to QBR decks. Focus: clear, unambiguous metric definitions (so CS + SRE + Product interpret the same numbers), quick queries to extract the signals, and a compact KPI table layout we can paste into customer-facing slides.

Scope:
- Primary SLIs used for renewal conversations and risk scoring: latency, uptime, cost/token (broken down by compute vs infra), cache hit rate.
- Measurement windows: 30d rolling for trend, 7d rolling for recent, and 1d for incident triage.
- Intended audience: CS managers prepping QBRs, SRE on-call for ex-post analysis, product PMs for prioritization.

Core definitions (single-line operational versions we use in QBRs):
1) Latency (response tail and central tendency)
   - Definition: observed end-to-end server-side time from request-received to first-token-emitted (ms). Client network time excluded (we use server-side ingress/egress).
   - Metrics we report: P50, P95, P99 (ms).
   - Windowing: 7d rolling for P50/P95, 30d for P99 context.
   - Query hint (pseudo-SQL):
     SELECT model_variant, percentile(latency_ms, 50) as p50, percentile(latency_ms,95) as p95, percentile(latency_ms,99) as p99
     FROM inference_logs WHERE account_id = :acct AND ts >= now() - interval '7 day'
   - Notes: exclude warm-up synthetic traffic and streaming-chunk-subsequent latency (report only first-token latency for compare-to-SLA).

2) Uptime / Availability
   - Definition: percentage of requests that completed successfully (2xx or 3xx) without hitting provisioned-capacity or model-fallback errors. Computed as (successful_requests / total_healthcheckable_requests) * 100.
   - SLI window: 30d rolling; SLA buckets: Bronze=99.0, Silver=99.5, Gold=99.9 (example tiers).
   - Event types counted as failures: 5xx, timeouts (server-side), quota-deny, model-mismatch fallback (if fallback produces lower-quality variant and the policy marks as degraded).
   - Quick calc: count(status_code >= 500 OR timeout = true OR fallback_reason IS NOT NULL) as failures.

3) Cost per token (C/token)
   - Definition: amortized cost per user-visible output token = (inference_compute_cost + memory + infra-overhead + caching amortization) / output_tokens.
   - Breakdown fields we calculate and show: GPU-hours cost (per model-variant), storage/KV cost (for cache), networking egress amortized, and regional premium adjustments.
   - Windowing: 30d rolling spend divided by 30d rolling output tokens. Also show median prompt-length impact bucketed by 0-64,65-512,513-2048 tokens.
   - Query hint: use job-level compute_cost_usd from billing table joined to response tokens per request.

4) Cache hit rate
   - Definition: fraction of requests that served >= X% of the output prefix from KV/prefix cache (X usually 80%) OR where prefix-cache avoided the first N decoder steps. Operationally: cache_hits / cache_eligible_requests.
   - Two flavors: prefix-cache hit (reduces decoder steps) and response-cache hit (full response reuse). We report both.
   - Measurement: we mark a request with cache_type = 'prefix'|'response'|'none' and cache_coverage_percent.
   - Windowing: 7d rolling for cache-hit trends, show hourly heatmap for last 72h for incidents.

Signal-quality and filtering rules (how we clean data for QBRs):
- Exclude synthetic test traffic (label: test_traffic=true).
- Exclude internal-batch jobs (label: internal_batch=true).
- For latency P99, remove startup noise by excluding first 6h after deployment/version-change.
- For cache metrics, only include requests marked cache_eligible = true (some requests are intentionally not cacheable due to privacy/tooling).

KPI table template (copy/paste to QBR slide) - compact rows, one per metric-group. Columns: metric_id | quick_def | target | 30d_current | 7d_trend | action/owner
- LAT-FTT | first-token latency P95 (ms) | <= 300 ms | 380 ms | improving (-12%) | SRE: autoscale tune
- LAT-FULL | full-response latency median (ms) | <= 800 ms | 920 ms | flat (+2%) | Product: prompt-length reduction
- UP-AVAIL | availability (30d) | >= 99.5% | 99.72% | stable | CS/SRE joint
- COST/TKN | cost per output token (USD) | <$0.002 | $0.0028 | up (+18%) | Solutions Eng: enable model-quantize trial
- CACHE-PCT | prefix-cache hit rate (7d) | >= 40% | 32% | down (-9%) | Dev: recommend caching policy tweak

Risk thresholds and renewal triggers (operationalized):
- Yellow (monitor): any metric misses target by 10–25% over 30d.
- Red (action required, customer outreach): misses by >25% OR repeated short SLO bursts (>=3 incidents in 30d).
- Auto-notify: if availability < tier SLA for 24h continuous, webhook to CS + oncall slack channel + scheduled sync.

Playbook snippets (for CS to lead during QBR prep):
1) Data pull (2–3 days before QBR)
   - Run the 30d and 7d baseline queries (place results in shared sheet). Attach raw percentiles and token-distribution histogram.
   - Ask SRE to confirm any deployments or infra changes in the 30d window.
2) Root-cause annotation (1 day before)
   - If P95 elevated, annotate whether cause = model-size increase, token-length shift, batching policy change, or infra regen. Link to infra incident if present.
3) Slide build (same day)
   - Use the KPI table template above. Add a 1-line "why it moved" with owner and next-step. Keep slide copy < 3 bullets.

Example: quick queries and mapping to tables
- Latency: inference_logs(latency_ms, ts, model_variant, account_id, is_stream)
- Availability: request_outcomes(ts, account_id, status_category, failure_reason)
- Cost: billing_jobs(job_id, account_id, model_variant, compute_cost_usd, io_cost_usd, start_ts) JOIN responses(job_id, output_tokens)
- Cache: cache_events(ts, account_id, cache_type, coverage_pct, cache_eligible)

Unresolved questions / decisions for product & SRE:
- Do we standardize on first-token latency P95 as the canonical latency metric for QBRs? (pros: aligns with user-perceived latency for streaming; cons: ignores total wait for long responses)
- Should cache hit rate target be account-weighted or request-weighted? (we currently use request-weighted, propose switching to token-weighted for fairness)

Notes-to-self / ephemeral items (keeps doc informal):
- Pulling tokenization library version is annoyingly manual — add instrumentation so cost per token uses the exact tokenizer hash.
- Consider adding a small cell in the KPI table showing 'median prompt tokens' to explain cost swings.

Appendix: example raw KPI row (CSV-friendly)
metric_id,account_id,window_start,window_end,target,current_value,trend_pct,owner,notes
LAT-FTT,acct-532,2025-12-11,2026-01-10,<=300,380,-12%,SRE-ops,"P95 impacted by 2025-12-22 model rollout"

If you want, I can also generate the exact SQL/PromQL versions for our monitoring stacks and a small sample sheet (CSV) that CS can upload to the QBR slide deck.

END
